title: Canada Names the Pathways Behind Its 200,000 Extra PR Spaces for 2027
excerpt: IRCC will fill the one-time 2027 spaces from applications already in the system: provincial nominee workers and closed economic programs in one cohort of 100,000, and family and humanitarian cases in the other.
body:
• Canada has named the pathways that will fill its 200,000 extra in-Canada permanent residence spaces for 2027, published by IRCC on November 5, 2026.
  • Up to 100,000 spaces go to workers: people eligible through the Provincial Nominee Program and applicants waiting under closed programs including the Start-up Visa, Self-Employed Persons, Agri-Food Pilot and home care worker pathways.
  • The other 100,000 cover family and humanitarian cases: spouses, partners and children who have already applied, Hong Kong and Ukraine pathway applicants, and humanitarian and compassionate applicants approved in principle.
  • If you already have an application in one of these streams, you do not need to apply separately or take any additional steps to be considered.

Canada has filled in the details of its one-time measure to move up to 200,000 people already living in Canada to permanent residence in 2027. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) published the eligible pathways on a new government page, "Managing a responsive and predictable immigration system," on November 5, 2026, the same day Budget 2026 first announced the measure, CIC News reported.

How the 200,000 spaces split

The measure, called the 2027 TR-to-PR transition measures, runs in two cohorts of up to 100,000 spaces each, and sits on top of the annual permanent resident admissions target of 380,000 for 2027. It is not a new pathway and will not increase admissions on a recurring basis, the government says on its IRCC measures page.

For the workers cohort, the spaces go to workers already in communities outside Quebec, and their families, who are either eligible to apply for permanent residence through the Provincial Nominee Program or waiting for a decision under select programs that are now closed to new applications. IRCC names the Start-up Visa Program, the Self-Employed Persons Program, the Agri-Food Pilot and the home care worker (caregiver) pathways.

For the humanitarian cohort, the government aims to process all remaining applications under the permanent residence pathways for Hong Kong residents, which closed on August 31, 2026, and the pathway for Ukrainian nationals with family members in Canada, which closed on October 22, 2024. The cohort also covers in-Canada humanitarian and compassionate applicants whose applications have already been approved in principle, and spouses, common-law partners and children of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who have already applied and are awaiting a final decision.

What this means if you are waiting

The deciding feature of the measure is that it works from applications already in the system. "Applicants do not need to apply separately or take any additional steps to be considered under these measures," IRCC states. CIC News likewise notes that qualifying foreign nationals do not need to take any action to be considered under the 2027 measures.

That cuts both ways. A temporary resident in Canada whose application sits in one of the named streams — a provincial nominee candidate, a caregiver-pathway applicant, a sponsored spouse waiting in Canada — is in line for the extra processing space. A worker or student who has not applied under any of these pathways gains nothing directly from this announcement, because no new intake opens with it.

Why Ottawa is doing it

IRCC frames the measure as a reset tool: the extra space is meant to give stability to people already in communities across Canada, fulfil previous humanitarian commitments, and reduce application inventories and processing times. The pathways named are, in large part, backlogs — closed programs whose applicants have been waiting for decisions, in some cases for years.

The measure applies for one year, 2027, and the workers cohort excludes Quebec, which runs its own selection. Readers with a pending application in a named stream need take no step now; those considering Canada should treat the announcement as backlog clearance, not a new route in.
